1// Note: This is a copy of the arithmetic decoder from `hayro-jpeg2000`,
2// keep the two in sync.
3
4//! The arithmetic decoder, described in Annex C.
5//!
6//! The arithmetic decoder keeps track of some state and continuously receives
7//! context labels as input, each time yielding a new bit from the original data
8//! as output.
9
10pub(crate) struct ArithmeticDecoder<'a> {
11    /// The underlying encoded data.
12    data: &'a [u8],
13    /// The C-register (see Table C.1).
14    c: u32,
15    /// The A-register (see Table C.1).
16    a: u32,
17    /// The pointer to the current byte.
18    base_pointer: u32,
19    /// The bit shift counter.
20    shift_count: u32,
21}
22
23impl<'a> ArithmeticDecoder<'a> {
24    pub(crate) fn new(data: &'a [u8]) -> Self {
25        let mut decoder = ArithmeticDecoder { data, c: 0, a: 0, base_pointer: 0, shift_count: 0 };
26
27        decoder.initialize();
28
29        decoder
30    }
31
32    /// Read the next bit using the given context label.
33    #[inline(always)]
34    pub(crate) fn read_bit(&mut self, context: &mut ArithmeticDecoderContext) -> u32 {
35        self.decode(context)
36    }
37
38    /// The INITDEC procedure from C.3.5.
39    ///
40    /// We use the version from Annex G in <https://www.itu.int/rec/T-REC-T.88-201808-I>.
41    fn initialize(&mut self) {
42        self.c = ((self.current_byte() as u32) ^ 0xff) << 16;
43        self.read_byte();
44
45        self.c <<= 7;
46        self.shift_count -= 7;
47        self.a = 0x8000;
48    }
49
50    /// The BYTEIN procedure from C.3.4.
51    ///
52    /// We use the version from Annex G from <https://www.itu.int/rec/T-REC-T.88-201808-I>.
53    #[inline(always)]
54    fn read_byte(&mut self) {
55        if self.current_byte() == 0xff {
56            let b1 = self.next_byte();
57
58            if b1 > 0x8f {
59                self.shift_count = 8;
60            } else {
61                self.base_pointer += 1;
62                self.c = self.c.wrapping_add(0xfe00).wrapping_sub((self.current_byte() as u32) << 9);
63                self.shift_count = 7;
64            }
65        } else {
66            self.base_pointer += 1;
67            self.c = self.c.wrapping_add(0xff00).wrapping_sub((self.current_byte() as u32) << 8);
68            self.shift_count = 8;
69        }
70    }
71
72    /// The RENORMD procedure from C.3.3.
73    #[inline(always)]
74    fn renormalize(&mut self) {
75        // Original code:
76        // loop {
77        //     if self.shift_count == 0 {
78        //         self.read_byte();
79        //     }
80        //
81        //     self.a <<= 1;
82        //     self.c <<= 1;
83        //     self.shift_count -= 1;
84        //
85        //     if self.a & 0x8000 != 0 {
86        //         break;
87        //     }
88        // }
89
90        // Optimization: Batch shifts.
91        while self.a & 0x8000 == 0 {
92            if self.shift_count == 0 {
93                self.read_byte();
94            }
95
96            let shifts_needed = self.a.leading_zeros() - 16;
97            let batch = shifts_needed.min(self.shift_count);
98            self.a <<= batch;
99            self.c <<= batch;
100            self.shift_count -= batch;
101        }
102    }
103
104    /// The `LPS_EXCHANGE` procedure from C.3.2.
105    #[inline(always)]
106    #[allow(unused, reason = "for reference")]
107    fn exchange_lps(&mut self, context: &mut ArithmeticDecoderContext, qe_entry: &QeData) -> u32 {
108        // Original code:
109        // let d;
110        //
111        // if self.a < qe_entry.qe {
112        //     self.a = qe_entry.qe;
113        //     d = context.mps;
114        //     context.index = qe_entry.nmps;
115        // } else {
116        //     self.a = qe_entry.qe;
117        //     d = 1 - context.mps;
118        //
119        //     if qe_entry.switch {
120        //         context.mps = 1 - context.mps;
121        //     }
122        //
123        //     context.index = qe_entry.nlps;
124        // }
125
126        // Branchless version, shows better performance.
127
128        let cond = (self.a < qe_entry.qe) as u32;
129        let inv_cond = 1 - cond;
130
131        self.a = qe_entry.qe;
132        // d = if cond { mps } else { 1 - mps }
133        let d = context.mps() ^ inv_cond;
134        // flip mps only when !cond && switch
135        context.xor_mps(inv_cond & (qe_entry.switch as u32));
136        // index = if cond { nmps } else { nlps }
137        let cond_u8 = cond as u8;
138        let inv_cond_u8 = inv_cond as u8;
139        context.set_index(cond_u8 * qe_entry.nmps + inv_cond_u8 * qe_entry.nlps);
140
141        d
142    }
143
144    /// The `MPS_EXCHANGE` procedure from C.3.2.
145    #[inline(always)]
146    #[allow(unused, reason = "for reference")]
147    fn exchange_mps(&mut self, context: &mut ArithmeticDecoderContext, qe_entry: &QeData) -> u32 {
148        // Original code:
149        //  let d;
150        //
151        //  if self.a < qe_entry.qe {
152        //      d = 1 - context.mps;
153        //
154        //      if qe_entry.switch {
155        //          context.mps = 1 - context.mps;
156        //      }
157        //
158        //      context.index = qe_entry.nlps;
159        //  } else {
160        //      d = context.mps;
161        //      context.index = qe_entry.nmps;
162        //  }
163
164        // Branchless version, shows better performance.
165        let cond = (self.a < qe_entry.qe) as u32;
166        let inv_cond = 1 - cond;
167        // d = if cond { 1 - mps } else { mps }
168        let d = context.mps() ^ cond;
169        // flip mps only when cond && switch
170        context.xor_mps(cond & (qe_entry.switch as u32));
171        // index = if cond { nlps } else { nmps }
172        let cond_u8 = cond as u8;
173        let inv_cond_u8 = inv_cond as u8;
174        context.set_index(cond_u8 * qe_entry.nlps + inv_cond_u8 * qe_entry.nmps);
175        d
176    }
177
178    /// The DECODE procedure from C.3.2.
179    ///
180    /// We use the version from Annex G from <https://www.itu.int/rec/T-REC-T.88-201808-I>.
181    #[inline(always)]
182    pub(crate) fn decode(&mut self, context: &mut ArithmeticDecoderContext) -> u32 {
183        let qe_entry = &QE_TABLE[context.index() as usize];
184
185        self.a -= qe_entry.qe;
186
187        // Old code:
188        // let d;
189        //
190        // if (self.c >> 16) < self.a {
191        //     if self.a & 0x8000 == 0 {
192        //         d = self.exchange_mps(context, qe_entry);
193        //         self.renormalize();
194        //     } else {
195        //         d = context.mps();
196        //     }
197        // } else {
198        //     self.c -= self.a << 16;
199        //
200        //     d = self.exchange_lps(context, qe_entry);
201        //     self.renormalize();
202        // }
203        //
204        // d
205
206        // This is a faster version that reduces branching, which has shown
207        // itself to be the main limiting factor for better performance.
208        // We short-circuit the case where just the most probably symbol is
209        // returned, and otherwise use a code path that works for both,
210        // MPS_EXCHANGE and LPS_EXCHANGE.
211
212        if (self.c >> 16) < self.a && self.a & 0x8000 != 0 {
213            return context.mps();
214        }
215
216        // Unified branchless MPS_EXCHANGE / LPS_EXCHANGE.
217        //
218        // Compare with exchange_mps and exchange_lps above — the only
219        // difference between them is that LPS flips the role of cond:
220        //   exchange_mps: d = mps ^ cond,       flip when cond,      index = cond*nlps + inv*nmps
221        //   exchange_lps: d = mps ^ inv_cond,   flip when inv_cond,  index = cond*nmps + inv*nlps
222        //
223        // This is equivalent to XOR-ing cond with is_lps, so we can handle
224        // both paths with a single branchless computation.
225        //
226        // As can be seen above, renormalization is always performed.
227        let is_lps = ((self.c >> 16) >= self.a) as u32;
228
229        // LPS: C -= A << 16 (no-op when MPS).
230        let lps_mask = is_lps.wrapping_neg(); // 0xFFFF_FFFF if LPS, 0 if MPS
231        self.c -= (self.a << 16) & lps_mask;
232
233        // Same condition as in exchange_mps / exchange_lps.
234        let cond = (self.a < qe_entry.qe) as u32;
235
236        // LPS: a = qe (no-op when MPS, a stays as a - qe).
237        self.a = (self.a & !lps_mask) | (qe_entry.qe & lps_mask);
238
239        // exchange_mps: d = mps ^ cond       →  cond ^ 0
240        // exchange_lps: d = mps ^ inv_cond   →  cond ^ 1
241        // unified:      d = mps ^ (cond ^ is_lps)
242        let d = context.mps() ^ cond ^ is_lps;
243
244        // exchange_mps: flip mps when cond & switch       →  (cond ^ 0) & switch
245        // exchange_lps: flip mps when inv_cond & switch   →  (cond ^ 1) & switch
246        // unified:      flip mps when (cond ^ is_lps) & switch
247        context.xor_mps((cond ^ is_lps) & (qe_entry.switch as u32));
248
249        // exchange_mps: index = cond * nlps + inv_cond * nmps
250        // exchange_lps: index = cond * nmps + inv_cond * nlps  (swapped)
251        // unified: the result is always exactly nmps or nlps —
252        //          pick nlps when (cond ^ is_lps) == 1, nmps otherwise.
253        let pick_nlps = ((cond ^ is_lps) as u8).wrapping_neg(); // 0xFF or 0x00
254        context.set_index(qe_entry.nmps ^ ((qe_entry.nmps ^ qe_entry.nlps) & pick_nlps));
255
256        self.renormalize();
257
258        d
259    }
260
261    #[inline(always)]
262    fn current_byte(&self) -> u8 {
263        self.data
264            .get(self.base_pointer as usize)
265            .copied()
266            // "The number of bytes corresponding to the coding passes is
267            // specified in the packet header. Often at that point there are
268            // more symbols to be decoded. Therefore, the decoder shall extend
269            // the input bit stream to the arithmetic coder with 0xFF bytes,
270            // as necessary, until all symbols have been decoded."
271            .unwrap_or(0xFF)
272    }
273
274    #[inline(always)]
275    fn next_byte(&self) -> u8 {
276        self.data.get((self.base_pointer + 1) as usize).copied().unwrap_or(0xFF)
277    }
278}
279
280// Previously, we stored the context as 2 u32's, but doing it with a bit-packed
281// u8 seems to be slightly better (though it doesn't make that huge of a
282// difference).
283/// Bits 0-6 = index (0-46).
284/// Bit 7 = mps (0 or 1).
285#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, Default)]
286pub(crate) struct ArithmeticDecoderContext(u8);
287
288impl ArithmeticDecoderContext {
289    #[inline(always)]
290    pub(crate) fn index(self) -> u32 {
291        (self.0 & 0x7F) as u32
292    }
293
294    #[inline(always)]
295    pub(crate) fn mps(self) -> u32 {
296        (self.0 >> 7) as u32
297    }
298
299    #[inline(always)]
300    fn set_index(&mut self, index: u8) {
301        self.0 = (self.0 & 0x80) | index;
302    }
303
304    #[inline(always)]
305    fn xor_mps(&mut self, val: u32) {
306        self.0 ^= ((val & 1) << 7) as u8;
307    }
308}
309
310#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
311struct QeData {
312    qe: u32,
313    nmps: u8,
314    nlps: u8,
315    switch: bool,
316}
317
318macro_rules! qe {
319    ($($qe:expr, $nmps:expr, $nlps:expr, $switch:expr),+ $(,)?) => {
320        [
321            $(
322                QeData {
323                    qe: $qe,
324                    nmps: $nmps,
325                    nlps: $nlps,
326                    switch: $switch,
327                }
328            ),+
329        ]
330    };
331}
